overview.doc: The organisation header for everyone, the inventory for admins. Any member gets the organisation row with its department / workspace / member COUNTS plus their own role (owner | admin | member) - it is their own organisation and the counts are aggregate. The department list and the workspace list are returned ONLY to a caller at dom_admin_security or above: both are scoped by domain_id alone, so they carry the name and member count of every workspace in the org including private ones the caller cannot open - handing those to a plain member disclosed a list they had no access to and could not act on. Filtering per caller is not viable here: per-workspace membership lives in each hub's own database, which is why yp.workspace_members is a count-only rollup. Workspace rows carry desk.home column names (hub_id, home_id, filename, area, filetype) so the org view opens one through the same client helper the desk's home grid uses. A caller still on the default public domain has no organisation and gets nulls plus empty lists, not an error. can_manage reports whether THIS caller may run the department mutations below; can_browse reports whether the client should offer the org view at all - reported rather than inferred from an empty list, because 'no departments yet' and 'not allowed to see them' must not render alike.

organisation.doc: Org row plus department_count, workspace_count and member_count. null outside an organisation.

role.doc: owner (>= dom_owner) | admin (>= dom_admin_security) | member (everything below, including privilege 0). null outside an organisation.

departments.doc: Departments in rank order with counts. EMPTY for a caller below dom_admin_security. Empty departments ARE included for those who may see them - the design draws them as a header with no grid.

workspaces.doc: Every workspace in the domain, department_id null for ungrouped. EMPTY for a caller below dom_admin_security.

can_manage.doc: 1 when the caller may add / rename / delete departments (>= dom_admin)

can_browse.doc: 1 when the caller may see departments and workspaces (>= dom_admin_security)

my_departments.doc: The departments the CALLER can see, each with its workspaces - what the topbar's department crumb, its 'Switch Departments' list and the department-scoped workspace switcher draw. A caller at dom_admin_security or above gets every department of the organisation (empty ones included) and every workspace in them, the same inventory overview hands them. Anyone below that gets only the departments they have a workspace in, and only those workspaces, read from their OWN membership (yp.my_departments) - never a workspace name they could not open. Ungrouped workspaces are not listed: they have no department to draw. Outside an organisation the list is empty, not an error.

departments.doc: [{id, name, rank, workspaces:[desk.home-shaped rows]}] in rank order

can_manage.doc: 1 when the caller may add / rename / delete departments (>= dom_admin)

rename.doc: Rename the organisation - the pencil beside its name in the org dropdown. Changes the DISPLAY NAME only. Deliberately not organization.update, which also calls domain_update and would rewrite yp.domain.name to '<ident>.<main_domain>' - a no-op on a healthy row but a corrupted address on one whose ident is NULL. Org-admin only, same gate as the department mutations.

department_add.doc: Create a department inside the caller's organisation. Org-admin only: the ACL entry checks the caller owns the hub they addressed, and the worker then requires domain privilege >= Remit.dom_admin through domain_privilege - the same gate organisation.update uses.

name.doc: Department name, unique within the organisation

rank.doc: Display order - appended after the existing departments

department_rename.doc: Rename a department. Domain-scoped in SQL as well as here: department_id is matched together with the caller's domain_id, so an id belonging to another tenant is refused rather than renamed.

department_remove.doc: Delete a department WITHOUT deleting its workspaces. The member workspaces have their department_id unset and reappear in the org view's ungrouped row; the response reports how many moved. This is why yp.department carries no foreign key to yp.hub - a cascade here would destroy real workspaces because somebody tidied a grouping.

department_assign.doc: Move one workspace into a department (the workspace arrives as `nid`; `hub_id` is the caller's own hub and is what the ACL reads for scope, exactly as in desk.leave_hub), or out of every department when department_id is empty or absent - that is how a workspace becomes ungrouped without the department being deleted, so an empty value is a legitimate target and not a missing argument. Changes no permission, no address and no storage: department is a label on the organisation's side of the world.

nid.doc: Workspace to move - yp.hub.id. NOT hub_id, which addresses the caller's own hub.

department_id.doc: Target department, or empty to make the workspace ungrouped

setup_state.doc: Whether the caller's organisation has been through the 'Set up your organization' wizard (organisation.metadata.$.org_setup_done), its department count and the caller's role / can_manage - what the desk weighs before offering the wizard. Outside an organisation: setup_done 1 (nothing to set up).

setup_done.doc: unix time it was finished or skipped, 0 if never
Record that the organisation's setup wizard was finished or skipped, so it is not offered again. Org-admin only (>= dom_admin), same gate as the department mutations.

Org admins (>= dom_admin).
